correctness.rationale: The split quadratic-root normal form from Ciliberto et al. yields a degree-two lambda=N/D unramified above 0,1,infinity: the zeros of D,N,D-N are reduced and disjoint. Conversely the associated model for every such lambda has precisely six transverse root collisions, hence six I2 fibres (also at infinity when relevant, by homogeneous divisors), and chi=1 with a section gives rationality. For the degree-six Legendre J, the indices are 3 at eta_± and 2 at each harmonic point and each pole; these exhaust its Riemann–Hurwitz sum of 10. The chain rule then makes Belyi equivalent to the two distinct branch values of lambda lying in the five allowed non-pole points. For each unordered branch pair there is one quadratic cover modulo source automorphism. The anharmonic group acts as S3 on harmonic points and by sign on the two eta values; in particular the stabilizer of a harmonic point swaps the eta values, proving the one mixed orbit. The three pair types therefore suffice. The generic j is nonconstant; equal j after a base change gives at most a quadratic twist. An odd valuation gives I0* or I2* from a smooth fibre or an I2 respectively, so the twist preserving six I2 and no other singular fibres has even valuations, and is square in C(t). Minimal regular models then give the required zero-preserving isomorphism. For the chosen N and D the critical values are u,v; each chosen eta merges its contribution (3,3) to 6, each chosen harmonic value merges (2,2) to 4, and the poles stay 2^6. The three passports differ and each contributes total ramification 22. This is a composition of j-functions, not an assertion that the raw untwisted Legendre base change has the required fibre types.
residual_risks: The scope is zero-section-preserving elliptic fibrations over C, not abstract rational surfaces, not fields of positive characteristic and not arithmetic isomorphism.

evidence: The general six-I2 normal form covers the whole family, but the inspected passage does not classify its Belyi locus.
A rational elliptic surface has rank 10 in its Néron–Severi group, so six I2 give Mordell–Weil rank 2 by Shioda–Tate, not the extremal rank 0.
Ordinary modular maps to X(1) have indices at most 3 and 2 over the elliptic values, whereas each passport here exceeds one of those bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The comparison excludes mechanical coverage by the ordinary modular quotient and extremal surface lists; general normal form gives the space to classify, not which members satisfy the branching requirement.

evidence: The prior normal form allows quadratic lambda with freely varying distinct branch values away from 0,1,infinity.
For the claimed property those values are restricted to a five-point set, giving 1+3+6 pairs before quotienting. The orbit count and twist uniqueness are needed to get exactly three fibrations.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of the compared statements gives the relevant equivalence classes by parameter substitution. A passport match alone without the appropriate rational source, Legendre factorization or twist condition would not establish this classification.

evidence: The underlying map problem is a composite rational Belyi map J composed with a quadratic, with six poles of order two; admissible elliptic fibration twists are unique.
The related Resultary Fermat-circle fibration has degree twelve but fibres I4+2I2+4I1; the composite genus-one examples differ in genus and passport.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A classification of these particular decomposable genus-zero Belyi maps would materially cover the claim via twist uniqueness. Genus-one-source maps or j-maps with another pole partition do not do so. The raw Legendre family need not have the required singular fibres before twisting.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These accessible exact data sources are not tables of the three required rational maps or the six-I2 surface classes; degree, source genus and all partitions matter. This does not rule out other dessin catalogues.

originality.rationale: The supported claim is the complete degree-twelve Belyi locus in the six-I2 fibration family with models and passports. The normal form and the Legendre quotient are prior ingredients. The classification adds the quadratic branch restriction and orbit calculation and connects the maps to uniquely admissible elliptic fibrations; it does not claim new general theory of Belyi maps.
residual_risks: The full Beukers–Montanus chapter was not available for statement-level comparison; an implicit construction is not excluded.
Other dessins catalogues and older composite-map classifications may contain relevant cases; bounded comparisons are not proof of global priority.

value.rationale: The Belyi condition picks a naturally motivated finite sublocus of a known positive-dimensional six-I2 family. Counting it up to actual fibration isomorphism, giving models, and separating the three types by local ramification goes beyond exhibiting sample maps or identifying the ambient normal form. It provides a usable classification in both elliptic-surface and dessin terms.
residual_risks: No claim of full degree-12 dessin classification or novelty of the separate Legendre and quadratic covering constructions.
